clue.text: The average fellow will show forgiveness

blocks.note: par is the standard or average level
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap turns out to be the forgiving sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardon is an act of excusing an offence, the same thing as granting forgiveness.

clue.text: Throw stick out

blocks.note: first meaning: to hurl or cast forward
second meaning: to jut or protrude

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to throw a stick away; really two separate verbs are defined.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means both to propel something forward and to protrude beyond a surface.

clue.text: Concerned with its poor attempt to get through again?

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the word beside it is badly put together and must be rearranged

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried student frets about a weak effort at passing an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second sitting of an examination for a candidate who failed the first time.

clue.text: Heads for old poem about bishop

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the old poem goes around the bishop

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a verse is a poem
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Leaders turn to an ancient poem about a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like a plural noun or a verb, but it is the side of a coin. B is the chess abbreviation for bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin is its main face, the side commonly called heads.

clue.text: Lady to travel round island slowly

indicators.note: to travel round something is to go all the way around it, so travelling encircles the island

blocks.note: Ada is a woman's name
to go is to travel
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A woman takes a leisurely tour around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb for travelling wraps around the island letter, and the woman's name goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical tempo marking meaning at a slow, leisurely pace.

clue.text: Got into gear

blocks.note: surface reading: shifted a vehicle into gear, or got started
setter's reading: gear is clothing, and one got into one's clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Gear is slang for clothes, so getting into gear means putting garments on.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on clothes, the informal sense of gear, is the act of clothing oneself.

clue.text: Prospective investment of food and money

blocks.note: grub is slang for food
a stake is money put up or wagered

explanation.surface: A potential venture involving funding for provisions and cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospective' is a pun: the investment is in a prospector, who was traditionally supplied with provisions in return for a share of any find.
explanation.definitionFit: A grubstake is supplies or funds advanced to a mining prospector in exchange for a share of profits.

clue.text: Each in public setting seen to swallow too much

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so each goes within the public word
a setting is a mount that holds a jewel, so public acts as the surround

blocks.note: overt means open and public
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Everyone eating at a public venue is observed gorging themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' reads as a venue, but it is a jewel's mount holding the abbreviation for each.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume more food than is needed, eating to excess.

clue.text: Down tools to make an impression

blocks.note: first meaning: to stop work in industrial action
second meaning: to hit or stamp, or to impress someone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests workers walking out to get noticed; 'down tools' is a British idiom for stopping work in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to withdraw labour as a protest and to impress, as when an idea strikes someone.

clue.text: Music that brings us to our feet

definitions.text: Music that brings us to our feet

blocks.clueFragment: Music that brings us to our feet
blocks.note: surface reading: a tune so exciting the audience leaps up to dance or cheer
setter's reading: the piece during which everyone is obliged to stand out of respect

explanation.walkthrough: The British national anthem is traditionally heard standing, so the music makes people rise from duty rather than delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The national anthem of the United Kingdom is the piece of music for which audiences customarily stand up.

clue.text: Improved ale with tuberculin tested injection

indicators.note: with joins the ale to the tested label that follows
an injection puts something inside a body, so the tested label goes into the ale

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
TT is the label for tuberculin-tested milk

explanation.surface: A beer has been enhanced by a dose of something medical.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuberculin-tested (TT) was a British label for milk from cattle checked for tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something better has been made superior or improved compared to before.

clue.text: Maintained unnatural tidiness

indicators.note: unnatural means not in its normal state, so the letters are put into an abnormal order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone kept up a level of neatness that seemed almost unhealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have insisted is to have asserted or maintained a claim firmly and persistently.

clue.text: Rush to get plugged into Stock Exchange framework

indicators.note: plugged into means placed inside, so the plugging word sits within the exchange letters
a framework surrounds and supports, so the exchange letters form a frame around the rest

blocks.note: SE is the abbreviation for Stock Exchange
tamped means packed down or plugged

explanation.surface: A frantic dash to get connected to the trading floor's systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugged into' sounds like being connected to a computer system; here plugged means packed down, as tobacco in a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of a crowd or herd.

clue.text: On being in control of a religious establishment

indicators.note: being in means sitting inside, so the little word goes within the word for control

blocks.note: mastery is command or control
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is now running a church institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On being in control' reads as one phrase about being in charge; the insertion splits the control word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a building where monks live in religious community, a kind of religious house.

clue.text: Shortage put right in the end

indicators.note: put signals placing one item somewhere, here inside the other
in tells where it is put: inside the phrase for the end

blocks.note: death is the end of life
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A deficiency that is finally corrected at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put right' looks like a phrase meaning fixed; split it, so R is put in DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something, which is a shortage.

clue.text: Pa can't manage on so little sleep

indicators.note: to manage letters is to handle and arrange them, so they are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Father cannot cope on so few hours of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage' has to be read as an instruction to rework the letters before it, not as coping.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a brief doze or short nap, a small amount of sleep.

clue.text: Got into a row for dodgy dealing

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone got into a quarrel over shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' wants to mean an argument, but here it is a line, as in things set out in a straight row.
explanation.definitionFit: Things aligned have been arranged in a straight line, set out in a neat row.

clue.text: A politically correct line, perhaps, might get the bird?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version, so the letters are one possible rearrangement of another word

blocks.note: taken as written
PC is the abbreviation for politically correct
taken as written

explanation.surface: Toeing a correct political line could get you jeered, or given the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: To get the bird is British slang for being booed off; here the bird is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a long beak and throat pouch.

clue.text: Cut paperwork at union meetings

blocks.note: surface reading: reducing the bureaucracy at trade union gatherings
setter's reading: a union is a marriage, and the cut-up paper is thrown over the couple at the wedding

explanation.walkthrough: The union is a wedding, not a trade union, and the paper is cut into tiny pieces rather than reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are thrown over a newly married couple at their wedding celebration.

clue.text: Areas devastated in wake of Conservative ruler

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order
in the wake of means following behind, so the word comes after the party letter

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.surface: Regions left ruined following a Tory leader's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title taken by Roman emperors, making it a word for an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: No society, for example, found expressing approval of the whole bunch

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for society
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Nobody in the club voiced approval of the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy, a bunch of flowers carried or worn.

clue.text: Politician left amid a show of grief to become a barrister

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the politician and left go inside the show of grief

blocks.note: a tear is a visible sign of sorrow
MP is Member of Parliament
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An MP leaves politics in tears to start a legal career.
explanation.walkthrough: Barristers in London belong to Inns of Court such as the Inner or Middle Temple, so a Templar can be a lawyer, not only a crusading knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Templar is a lawyer or student with chambers in the Temple, one of London's Inns of Court.

clue.text: Lose control of rising debts in slump

indicators.note: rising means going upwards, so in this light the debts word reads backwards
in means placed inside, so the reversed debts go within the slump word

blocks.note: a dive is a sudden slump, as in prices
a loss is money owed or gone, here standing for debts

explanation.surface: A borrower falls apart as mounting debts drag them into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose control' is the definition, as in dissolving into tears, not the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve, as in dissolving into tears or laughter, is to be overcome emotionally.

clue.text: Be sparing with shampoo initially, then set hair

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the shampoo word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to crimp is to set hair in small waves; then just orders the pieces

explanation.surface: Use only a little shampoo before styling your hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise and be frugal, spending as little as possible.

clue.text: Arrive at a stretch of the river

blocks.note: first meaning: to get to a place
second meaning: a straight length of a waterway

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like boaters arriving somewhere; the second sense is the noun for a section of river between bends.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to get to a destination; as a noun it is a section of water between bends.

clue.text: Road junction can be offering a two-way option

blocks.note: an interchange is a junction of major roads
able means one can do something

explanation.surface: A motorway junction that lets drivers go either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Interchangeable things can swap places with each other, so either one may stand for the other.

clue.text: Run in, breathing one's last and losing water

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so run goes within the phrase for breathing one's last

blocks.note: breathing your last is dying
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone at the point of death is becoming dehydrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run in' looks like a phrase on its own, but R goes in DYING to make D-R-YING.
explanation.definitionFit: Drying means having moisture removed, so the thing is gradually losing its water.

clue.text: Henry Percy broke the code

indicators.note: broke means smashed apart, so the name's letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Henry Percy cracked a secret message.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Percy (Harry Hotspur) is a famous name, but here only the H of Henry is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypher, also spelled cipher, is a secret system of writing or a coded message.
